'''Dawn M. E. Bowdish''', (born May 21, 1976) is a Canadian immunologist and currently a professor in the Department of Pathology and Molecular Medicine at [[McMaster University]] in [[Ontario]], [[Canada]]. 

==Career==
In 1999, she graduated from the [[University of Guelph]] with an Honours Bachelor of Science in microbiology. Bowdish obtained her PhD from the [[University of British Columbia]] in 2005.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Keeping grandparents and grandchildren together for as long as possible |url=https://brighterworld.mcmaster.ca/articles/keeping-grandparents-and-grandchildren-together-for-as-long-as-possible/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |language=en-US}}</ref> There, under the supervision of [[Robert E. W. Hancock]], she discovered the immunomodulatory role of the host defence peptide LL-37.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Bowdish D. M., Davidson D. J., Speert D. P., Hancock R. E. | year = 2004 | title = The human cationic peptide LL-37 induces activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase and p38 kinase pathways in primary human monocytes | journal = Journal of Immunology | volume = 172 | issue = 6| pages = 3758–65 | doi = 10.4049/jimmunol.172.6.3758 | pmid = 15004180 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author = Bowdish D.M., Davidson D. J., Lau Y.E., Lee K., Scott M. G., Hancock R. E. | year = 2005 | title = Impact of LL-37 on anti-infective immunity | journal = Journal of Leukocyte Biology | volume = 77 | issue = 4| pages = 451–9 | doi = 10.1189/jlb.0704380 | pmid = 15569695 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author = Bowdish D.M., Davidson D.J., Hancock R.E. | year = 2005 | title = A re-evaluation of the role of host defence peptides in mammalian immunity | journal = Current Protein & Peptide Science | volume = 6 | issue = 1| pages = 35–51 | doi = 10.2174/1389203053027494 | pmid = 15638767 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author = Bowdish D. M., Davidson D. J., Scott M. G., Hancock R. E. | year = 2005 | title = Immunomodulatory activities of small host defense peptides | journal = Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy | volume = 49 | issue = 5| pages = 1727–32 | doi = 10.1128/AAC.49.5.1727-1732.2005 | pmid = 15855488 | pmc=1087655}}</ref> Bowdish worked at the [[University of Oxford]] from 2005-2008 under the supervision of [[Siamon Gordon]] where she studied the role of [[MARCO]] in eliciting an immune response [[Mycobacterium tuberculosis]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal | author = Bowdish D.M., Sakamoto K., Kim M. J., Kroos M., Mukhopadhyay S., Leifer C. A., Tryggvason K., Gordon S., Russell D. G. | year = 2009 | title = MARCO, TLR2, and CD14 Are Required for Macrophage Cytokine Responses to Mycobacterial Trehalose Dimycolate and Mycobacterium tuberculosis | journal = PLOS Pathogens | volume = 5 | issue = 6| article-number = e1000474 | doi = 10.1371/journal.ppat.1000474 | pmid = 19521507 | pmc=2688075 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Bowdish was appointed to the Department of Pathology & Molecular Medicine at McMaster University in 2009. Since, Bowdish has uncovered how aging alters [[myeloid cells]] to increase susceptibility to [[pneumococcal pneumonia]],<ref>{{cite journal | author = Verschoor C. P., Johnstone J., Loeb M., Bramson J. L., Bowdish D. M. | year = 2014 | title = Anti-pneumococcal deficits of monocyte-derived macrophages from the advanced-age, frail elderly and related impairments in PI3K-AKT signaling | journal = Human Immunology | volume = 75 | issue = 12| pages = 1192–6 | doi = 10.1016/j.humimm.2014.10.004 | pmid = 25446401 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author = Verschoor C.P., Johnstone J., Millar J., Parsons R., Lelic A., Loeb M., Bramson J. L., Bowdish D. M. | year = 2014 | title = Alterations to the Frequency and Function of Peripheral Blood Monocytes and Associations with Chronic Disease in the Advanced-Age, Frail Elderly | journal = PLOS ONE | volume = 9 | issue = 8| article-number = e104522 | doi = 10.1371/journal.pone.0104522 | pmid = 25105870 | pmc=4126708| bibcode = 2014PLoSO...9j4522V | doi-access = free }}</ref> and demonstrated that age-associated gut microbe [[dysbiosis]] in mice increases age-associated inflammation.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Thevaranjan N., Puchta A., Schulz C., Naidoo A., Szamosi J. C., Verschoor C. P., Loukov D., Schenck L. P., Jury J., Foley K. P., Schertzer J. D., Larché M. J., Davidson D. J., Verdú E. F., Surette M. G., Bowdish D. M. E. | year = 2017 | title = Age-Associated Microbial Dysbiosis Promotes Intestinal Permeability, Systemic Inflammation, and Macrophage Dysfunction | journal = Cell Host & Microbe | volume = 21 | issue = 4| pages = 455–466 | doi = 10.1016/j.chom.2017.03.002 | pmid = 28407483 | pmc=5392495}}</ref>
